messages:
leo: Hey folks 44 I'm on day 3. Using Ubuntu 22.04, fish shell (config managed via dotfiles repo), asdf for runtimes (python/node), and direnv for per-project envs. Problem: when I open the project in VS Code devcontainer the asdf shims aren't picked up and direnv errors with "no interpreter found for .envrc". Locally outside container `which python` -> ~/.asdf/shims/python, but in the container it's /usr/bin/python. Any tips on fish+direnv+asdf quirks?
sarah: Welcome Leo! Two common items: 1) asdf for fish needs the fish shims in fish config and 2) devcontainer shells sometimes start non-login shells so zsh/zprofile vs fish config ordering matters. Are you using `config.fish` or `~/.config/fish/config.fish`?
leo: Using dotfiles that symlink into ~/.config/fish/config.fish. I had `set -x PATH $HOME/.asdf/shims $PATH` in there, but maybe it runs after direnv or the devcontainer's shell init.
mike: For fish specifically, asdf recommends adding to config.fish: 

```
set -gx PATH $HOME/.asdf/shims $HOME/.asdf/bin $PATH
status --is-interactive; and source $HOME/.asdf/completions/asdf.fish
```

Also ensure `asdf init fish` (or the snippet) runs before direnv is loaded so the shims exist when direnv tries to find interpreters.
leo: Ah, I only had the `set -gx PATH` in a file sourced by a plugin that runs later. Might reorder.
alex: Another gotcha: direnv will evaluate .envrc in the container environment. If your devcontainer uses root or a different user, the HOME differs and asdf shims won't be under that HOME. Check devcontainer.json remoteUser and mount points. In our infra devcontainers we set `remoteUser: jovyan` (or the proper username) and forward HOME.
leo: Good call 4 I was using the container's default user root. Changing remoteUser to my dev user fixed the HOME mismatch.
sarah: Also check direnv's `layout` helpers. If you used `use python` in .envrc, direnv will try to find python in PATH at eval time; if asdf isn't initialized yet direnv fails. Sequence should be: asdf init -> PATH shims present -> direnv allowed/eval. For fish, add this at the top of config.fish: 

```
# ensure asdf is available before direnv
set -gx PATH $HOME/.asdf/shims $HOME/.asdf/bin $PATH
. $HOME/.asdf/asdf.fish  # or source completions path
status --is-interactive; and eval (direnv hook fish)
```

mike: For VS Code devcontainers, also check the "useRemoteEnv" or `updateRemoteUserUID` settings and ensure the container build installs asdf and the plugin runtimes. If runtime binaries are only on the host, the container needs them provisioned in Dockerfile or via a repo script.
leo: The Dockerfile does install asdf and plugins during build, but I had omitted `ENV HOME=/home/dev` and the build created asdf under /root during image build steps. Oops. Rebuilt with proper HOME and it's better.
infra-bot: Created ticket IT-5012: "Devcontainer asdf+direnv sample: fish config snippet + remoteUser note" assigned to sarah.
alex: Pro tip: add a small check to .devcontainer/post-create to run `asdf reshim` and `direnv allow` so new clones don't hit this. Example in post-create: 
```
# post-create
export HOME=/home/dev
asdf reshim || true
direnv allow || true
```
leo: Added that to my branch, rebuilt, and now in-container `which python` -> ~/.asdf/shims/python and direnv no longer errors. Huge help, thanks all :party_parrot:
